extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and authors skeptical of prescriptive writing advice
extracted.subtask_description: Short opinion/advice piece urging fiction writers to reject universal 'rules' and instead make craft choices that suit each story, medium, and the writer's intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward universal writing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every claim someone makes about how fiction works can be rebutted with counterexamples."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat blanket rules about fiction as provisional, not authoritative. Expect counterexamples to any 'fundamental' rule and avoid applying prescriptions unthinkingly across different stories or objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match craft choices to story needs, medium, and intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Match craft choices to the specific story's needs, the medium's affordances, and the writer's intentions, not to received wisdom."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each decision (voice, structure, level of detail, pacing, etc.) by how well it serves the particular story and the platform/format you're using, and by what you intend to achieve emotionally or thematically, rather than by rote rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show vs. Tell is situational
rubrics_metrics.description: The common injunction 'show, don't tell' is not absolute; "telling is just as important as showing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use showing and telling as tools for different effects. Avoid the anti-pattern of blindly privileging one over the other; choose whichever technique best communicates the desired information, tone, or pacing for the scene or story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optionality of standard elements (character, plot, worldbuilding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supposedly fundamental elements — character, plot, worldbuilding — aren't actually mandatory in all successful fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume a story must include fully rounded characters, a conventional plot, or detailed worldbuilding. Consider omitting or minimizing elements when doing so better serves the piece; treat these elements as optional tools rather than checklist items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist dogmatic prescribing of craft rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece is written "for authors who don't want to follow rules." Resist dogmatic writing prescriptions (e.g., 'make your characters round').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of advice presented as immutable. The anti-pattern is following received wisdom by default; instead, test rules against your aims and the story's needs. Recognize that strategies advocated by conventional craft guides may be counterproductive in some contexts (e.g., flat characters or telling may be deliberate, effective choices).
